albums.blurb: The Meters were the house rhythm section for Allen Toussaint's New Orleans productions: guitarist Leo Nocentelli, keyboardist Art Neville, bassist George Porter Jr., and drummer Zigaboo Modeliste. Their all-instrumental 1969 debut on Josie Records, produced by Toussaint and Marshall Sehorn, distills spare, second-line syncopation into twelve short grooves, and "Cissy Strut" went on to become one of the most sampled recordings in popular music. It opened a run of eight albums that made them the definitive New Orleans funk band.
albums.reception: "Cissy Strut" reached No. 4 on the Billboard R&B chart and No. 23 on the Hot 100, and Billboard and Record World both named The Meters best R&B instrumental group in 1970.

albums.blurb: Jones's second Blue Note album, the follow-up to her 2002 debut Come Away with Me, was cut with her touring band and leans further into country and folk than its predecessor, with guest appearances by Dolly Parton on "Creepin' In" and The Band's Levon Helm and Garth Hudson. Its thirteen songs mix her own writing with material from Tom Waits, Townes Van Zandt, and Duke Ellington.
albums.reception: Feels Like Home sold about 1.02 million US copies in its first week, then the second-biggest SoundScan week ever by a female artist, and spent six consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 on its way to finishing as 2004's second-best-selling album.

albums.blurb: Judee Sill was a Los Angeles songwriter who described her Bach-inflected gospel-folk as "country-cult-baroque." This self-titled debut, released September 1971, was the first record ever issued on David Geffen's Asylum label, and its single "Jesus Was a Cross Maker," produced by Graham Nash, was later covered by The Hollies, Cass Elliot, and Warren Zevon. She released only one more album, Heart Food (1973), before her death in 1979.
albums.reception: Rolling Stone's Jon Landau hailed the album as one of the prettiest records of the year and Newsweek called Sill one of the most promising new singers in the business, but it sold poorly and never entered the Billboard 200.
